At an identical 8192MB budget and an identical plan CUBRID misses 342,384 times per statement (10.45% of 3,277,822 fixes) and PostgreSQL misses 0 (3,013,495 accesses, read=0), costing 1.160 vs 0.000 core-s of kernel page-cache read/copy, call-graph verified to the pgbuf_fix_release miss branch and 25.5% of the CPU excess. Scope widened from repeated sequential scans to random index-driven access. PostgreSQL's working set is MEASURED to fit (830,217 of 1,048,576 buffers, 20.8% headroom); CUBRID's is PROJECTED at 8,510 MiB heap-only against 8,192 MiB from a model validated on the PostgreSQL side to 1.6 pp, with its index term UNMEASURED because db_index exposes no page count.

A Q04 regression pin was added to its validation criteria.

headline_finding: The cross-engine pair is matched node-for-node on the dominant path: the same FK B-tree on lineitem.l_orderkey driven with exactly 456,771 probes on BOTH engines (CUBRID trace readkeys=456771, PostgreSQL 'Index Searches: 456771'), 1,825,856 rows on both, and identical intermediate cardinalities 300,270 / 456,771 / 1,825,856 / 72,985 confirmed by ground-truth count(*) queries both engines answer identically. imp_002_q05_relation: No steady-state cost on Q05 (0.87% miss rate, 65,169 of 7,524,219 fixes, zero device reads), but a NEW failure mode of the same replacement policy: the pool settles into a history-dependent equilibrium it cannot leave. Same query, data and plan measure 9.47-9.68 s on a native-only pool, 10.67-10.71 s carrying earlier workloads, and 13.27-13.55 s after ONE 24-statement USE_HASH full-scan block - stable over 60 further native statements and never self-recovering; only a server restart returns it. Miss counts across those states: 65,169 / 619,299 / ~1,631,608, a 25x swing. Cross-engine OS page-cache interference was tested and REJECTED at +0.71%.
imp_005_q05_relation: Second negative control, pinning the defect boundary from the other side: Q05 has the campaign's deepest scan_ptr chain (5 nested index scans) yet every trace counter is EXACT against ground truth (5 / 300,270 / 3,006,380 / 456,771 / 1,825,856 / 72,985), because the chain runs at degree 1 and never enters the parallel-worker stats merge. The defect requires BOTH a scan_ptr chain AND parallel workers, which makes it a hard sequencing dependency for IMP-009.
imp_009_summary: compute_parallel_degree() hardcodes an uncorrelated subquery's parallel degree to 1 at src/query/parallel/px_parallel.cpp:89-92 ('TODO: degree fixed at 1 (main + gather = 2) to be revised...') and explicitly discards an explicit hint at :99-103 ('hint ignored, degree fixed for subquery, ignore the parallelism parameter'). Q05's optimizer folds the whole region->nation->customer->orders->lineitem index-NL chain into such a subquery, so 99% of the query runs single-threaded while the trivial hash-join probe above it gets 4 workers. PostgreSQL's contrast: parallelism is a property of the plan BRANCH - allpaths.c:830 set_rel_consider_parallel (extended to subquery rels at :2919-2922), :608 generate_useful_gather_paths places the Gather above an arbitrary parallel-safe branch, and execParallel.c:1514 ParallelQueryMain -> :1583 ExecutorRun runs that whole branch in every worker, so nodeNestloop.c:61 ExecNestLoop needs no parallel variant. Confirmed by the source's own prediction: PARALLEL(6) 9.605 s, PARALLEL(12) 9.648 s, serial 9.716 s, native 9.615 s - a 1.1% band - with the trace showing 'parallel workers: 2' on the subquery under every hint. Direct upstream precedent: 978b628c8 [CBRD-26931] 'Parallelize uncorrelated scalar subquery inner scan' (#7316) fixed the same defect class for SCALAR subqueries after TPC-H Q15 regressed 12.2 s -> 24.2 s; Q05 is the non-scalar branch it did not cover. Difficulty high (hint-honouring first step: low). Risk medium, and IMP-005 must be fixed first or co-validated because raising the degree exposes Q05's 5-level scan_ptr chain to the (k-1)x counter multiplication for the first time.

counter_direction_note: Reported in both directions. (a) CUBRID parallelizes this scan BETTER than PostgreSQL: 5.31x on 6 units (88% efficiency) against 4.06x on 5+leader (68%), so the serial per-row cost ratio is 3.1297x - WORSE than the 2.4583x parallel-regime F_cpu - and CUBRID's better scaling claws back 1.27x. (b) PostgreSQL spends 14.75% = 1.338 core-s of its executor CPU on per-statement parallel-worker page-table setup and teardown plus 0.298 core-s of per-tuple memory-context churn, 1.636 core-s that CUBRID's threaded model does not pay at all; net of both, F_cpu would be 2.744x rather than 2.458x. (c) Both engines pay about 2.5 core-s to parallelize, for opposite reasons: CUBRID +2.500 core-s (66% its extra page-cache reads), PostgreSQL +2.585 core-s (63% worker fork/teardown). (d) The headline is a statement about a CONFIGURED comparison: at parallelism=12 CUBRID reaches 2.021 s, 1.917x faster than its contracted 3.875 s, and at max_parallel_workers_per_gather=11 PostgreSQL reaches 1.297 s. Neither is a ceiling. (e) CUBRID's IPC is HIGHER (2.30 vs 1.77): it is not stalling, it is executing 3.30x the instructions and executing them well.

imp_010_summary: NEW, P1, buffer/IO + parallelism, difficulty LOW, evidence direct A/B. Root cause: scan-resistance is a property of the fixing THREAD, not of the scan. pgbuf_unlatch_void_zone_bcb (src/storage/page_buffer.c:6845) branches on the fixing thread's LRU identity - at :6900-6918 a page goes to the TOP of that thread's PRIVATE list with pgbuf_bcb_register_hit_for_lru(), at :6934 otherwise to the MIDDLE of a round-robin SHARED list where pgbuf_get_victim_from_lru_list() (:9268) reclaims it almost immediately. A pooled parallel-query worker never has an identity: thread_entry_task.cpp:75-76 retire_context() sets private_lru_index = -1 and m_is_private_lru_enabled = false, :95 recycle_context() repeats it, and px_scan_task.cpp:94 propagates m_px_orig_thread_entry = m_parent_thread_p from the parent AND NOTHING ELSE. Only session.c:740 and server_support.c:2401,2437 ever assign one - i.e. the client transaction thread that serves a NO_PARALLEL_SCAN scan. PostgreSQL contrast: heapam.c:398-410 initscan() sets BAS_BULKREAD from rs_nblocks > NBuffers/4, :1340 sets SO_ALLOW_STRAT so each worker's own heap_beginscan builds its own 256 kB ring (freelist.c:426,442), and GetBufferFromRing/AddBufferToRing (:623,:702) recycle only pages the scan itself read - DOP-independent by construction, and StrategyGetBuffer (:184) is 1.73% of PostgreSQL's Q06 profile so the ring is provably active. Effect: 458,209 -> 158,930 reads/statement, -4.57 GiB of page-cache traffic, worth about 1.66 core-s of the 14.023 core-s excess (11.8%), independently bounded by CUBRID's measured 2.500 core-s parallel CPU inflation of which this is 66%. Fix: propagate the parent's private_lru_index at px_scan_task.cpp:94 beside the existing m_px_orig_thread_entry assignment and call the existing pgbuf_thread_variables_init(). LIMITATION recorded: /*+ PARALLEL(1) */ degenerates to the serial non-px path, so the one-pooled-worker control is unobtainable on this build; the mechanism claim rests on the source branch plus the DOP-flat step, and validation criterion 3 (DOP independence restored) is written to settle it.

second_finding: Going parallel silently discards CUBRID's own buffer scan-resistance. Same query, same 8 GiB pool, same 682,937-page relation: one scan thread reads 158,930 pages per statement - the 158,649-page arithmetic overflow to within 0.18%, i.e. the policy is OPTIMAL serially - while 3/6/12 pooled workers read 468,980/458,209/459,242 and the section 12 headline regime reads 608,510 (89.1% miss). PostgreSQL's DOP effect on the same measurement is 1.9% (76,987 serial vs 78,482 at DOP 5 against a predicted 76,552 overflow), because its scan-resistance is a per-scan BAS_BULKREAD ring rather than a per-thread LRU list.
